Regarding our high rating, we believe we have earned and been awarded this rating as a result of the large majority of those dining with having found the cleanliness, taste and quality of our food and pricing to represent great value. Taste is a personal matter and we appreciate our Banh Mi may cost a little more than one purchased at a “Street Push Cart,” or a local tattered “Table Cloth” restaurant, but this is a direct result of the authenticity and quality of ingredients we use in the construction and serving of our Banh Mi. Regarding a table cloth, we all know there are Table Cloths and Table Rags.
Please keep in mind that the original French/Vietnamese kitchen collaboration introducing the first Banh Mi to Saigon in 19th Century did not create a cheap sandwich. The original sandwich was constructed on a crisp French baguette with a quality pate spread and layered with high quality oven roasted meats and garnished with local greens. As a result of the quality ingredients used in the construction of the original Banh Mi, this made for an expensive sandwich and was primarily only consumed and affordable by the affluent. As such, the Banh Mi itself and the term Banh Mi became a dining status symbol recognized by all local diners. 
Subsequently over the years and due to the status of the Banh Mi, street cart vendors in order to reduce the price of the Banh Mi and reach the mass local market, designed a lower quality Banh Mi that called for using cheaper, lower quality materials. This action resulted in the serving of a lower priced soggy roll, using a lower quality pate fill that many a street vendor constructed around a composite type mystery meat filling. To supplement their product’s lack in flavor, many a street vendor then used a large portion of pickled vegetables to drown out the unwanted flavors resulting from poor storage and lack of refrigeration on the street and of course the lower quality ingredients in general. 
We, on the other hand, have elected to resurrect and serve an authentic Banh Mi that replicates the taste and quality originally introduced to Saigon in the 19th Century. This we have succeeded with by our constructing upon a crisp baguette, including a quality pate spread and then layering our Banh Mi with our slow oven roasted high quality meats. As opposed to the street vendor, we do not attempt to try and add flavor by smothering our Banh Mi with pickled vegetables. Thank you for your review and comments. We do understand that our authentic Banh Mi does differ significantly to the simplified street push-cart version sold on the sidewalk. 

Basically, we serve an authentic Banh Mi as was originally introduced to Saigon in the 19th Century. As this was over 200 years ago, most only know that the Banh Mi was a French - Vietnamese culinary effort. Little know that the original Banh Mi was a very high quality sandwich and rather expensive and only eaten by the affluent. The high cost of the Banh Mi was due to the fact that the sandwich was constructed on a crisp French baguette, layered with a very high quality roasted beef, chicken or pork and complemented with a very tasty savory pate. The sandwich was then finished with a variety of specially selected local greens accenting the release and flavors of the succulence of the roasted meat. 

Consequently, over the years, street merchants seeking to create a cheaper, less expensive product to sell to the masses, did away with the crisp French baguette and roasted meats and replaced fillings with a combination mystery meat and a gelatin mix that was then smothered with a heavy dose of pickled vegetables to add flavor. As we all know, "sandwich" is merely a name and the sandwich eaten from a street push-cart in the street definitely differs in taste to the authentic Banh MI we serve. 

As we all understand, flavor and taste is a personal matter and some diners may actually prefer a pickle flavor rather than that of a quality roasted meat. We thank you for your review and trust our rendering of some Banh Mi history proves of value to you.

GohH76
Dear Colin A,

Thank you for your review documenting that familiar flavors become one’s personal benchmark and preference. 

We very much appreciate this opportunity to share with you and other TripAdvisor readers, a greater understanding about Vietnamese food and Vietnam’s Banh Mi.

Firstly, as confirmation to the authenticity of our food, we at My Banh Mi are located in Vietnam, retain talented and experienced Vietnamese chefs and use only authentic Vietnamese spices and ingredients that we source daily. The focus of our chefs is directed to preparing and serving authentically prepared Vietnamese home cooked food just as their mothers had cooked for them as children.

Authentic Vietnamese food is considered by the “Gourmet or Foodie” as clean in taste meaning that the food is not overly seasoned so the spices used do not overpower the flavors of the meat, fish or vegetables being prepared. It is not surprising that visitors to Vietnam find the food different to that which they have experienced abroad, but please consider that in many countries outside of Vietnam, the Vietnamese operators in many cases must make do with substitute seasonings as the authentic seasoning are not available for import. 

For instance, even in Vietnam, authenticity is hard to find. Even with the current Banh Mi push-cart that offers a Banh Mi, layered with a composite “Look alike meat,” on a soft roll, and smothered in chili sauce and pickled vegetables to give it flavor. This is not authenticity, as it was basically the 19th Century French that introduced the Banh Mi to Saigon ….. but does it sound logical that the French would introduce a soft bread, chili, pickled vegetable sandwich to Vietnam as it is now? 

What changed the Banh Mi? The original and authentic Banh Mi was a quality sandwich of roasted meats layered on a crisp French baguette and garnished with fresh greens and a spread of an expensive pate. As such, this sandwich was an expensive status symbol that was dined upon only by the elite and affluent who could afford them. In recent years, street vendors in Vietnam, in order to reach a mass market, degraded the quality of the sandwich to lower the price. This replicates the fast food franchised operators in the west with the marketing of burgers, pizza, etc. Franchised food operators are not recognized as serving authentic or great tasting food. It is simply quick food for a pinch.

Similarly, Vietnamese food prepared in foreign countries outside of Vietnam can definitively be different from food prepared in Vietnam. We realize that we as individuals, train our palates to recognize what we consider as good tasting. This starts as a child with our mothers saying “Eat this honey…Mommy made it and it is delicious.” Delicious or not delicious, whatever it was, it grew on us. As such, individual good taste is all about familiarity and not necessarily about authenticity. 

We hope that you have the opportunity to frequent us once again and to again try our truly authentic Vietnamese food. We are very happy to know that we have pleased your daughter’s palate.

Wishing you and yours continued good health and happiness in the coming New Year.
